questions.q: What's the key scoping difference between var and let/const?
options: Both are block-scoped with no difference
Both are function-scoped with no difference
var is function-scoped; let/const are block-scoped
let/const are function-scoped; var is block-scoped
questions.explain: var is visible throughout the whole function it's declared in; let and const only exist inside the specific block where they're declared.

questions.q: What does an arrow function do differently with this compared to a regular function?
options: It always sets this to the global object
It behaves exactly like a regular function in every case
It throws an error if this is referenced at all
It inherits this lexically from the enclosing scope instead of having this determined by how it's called
questions.explain: An arrow function has no this of its own; it uses whatever this was in the scope where the arrow function was written.

questions.q: Why does referencing a let variable before its declaration line throw an error, while doing the same with a var does not?
options: let variables are deleted after use
let variables don't exist until their declaration is reached in the block, while var is hoisted and simply returns undefined early
var cannot be referenced at all before being assigned
There is no real difference; both throw the same error
questions.explain: var declarations are hoisted and initialized to undefined; let/const are not usable until their declaration line is actually reached.
